The pacing of the story feels very natural, balanced, and appropriate for its quiet, atmospheric tone. The story time (a single, brief ferry crossing across the Elbe) closely mirrors the real-world time it takes to read the text. By avoiding dramatic time compression, the author allows the mundane details—such as dislodging a branch, collecting fares, and the rhythmic clanking of a loose latch—to unfold in near real-time. This steady, unhurried rhythm immerses the reader in the foggy, cold November setting and reflects Ilse's stoic, routine-driven existence. This deliberate pacing makes the final moment, where she silently watches her phone ring until the screen goes dark, carry much more emotional weight.
